about: Proposed region definition for a detailed map of Bolivia, as one region for the whole country, with the nine departments listed as an alternative. A proposal for discussion (docs/REGIONS-BO.md); no code reads this file, and it does not ship.

codes.why: A bare BO collides with no US code in STATE_CODES (engine/address_search.py).
codes.alternative: ISO 3166-2:BO, one letter after the hyphen: BO-H, BO-L, BO-C, BO-O, BO-P, BO-T, BO-S, BO-B, BO-N.
codes.warning: OCHA COD-AB p-codes BO01-BO09 follow a different order from the ISO letters (BO01 is Chuquisaca, BO-H; BO02 is La Paz, BO-L). Join by name, not by position.
codes.verified: Not checked against the ISO site (iso.org/obp returned HTTP 403). The same nine codes were read in four other sources on 2026-11-21: Debian iso-codes 4.16.0 (iso_3166-2.json); the UN/LOCODE subdivision list via the datasets/un-locode mirror (data/subdivision-codes.csv, refreshed 2026-10-16); Natural Earth 5.1.1 admin-1 (iso_3166_2); geoBoundaries BOL ADM1 (shapeISO).
codes.names: Debian, UN/LOCODE and Natural Earth name BO-B "El Beni"; geoBoundaries and OCHA COD-AB say "Beni".

regions.name: Bolivia

box_source.dataset: OCHA COD-AB Bolivia (bol_admin0.geojson / bol_admin1.geojson from bol_admin_boundaries.geojson.zip), source Ministerio de Desarrollo Rural y Tierras, version v02, valid_on 2024-09-16, files last modified 2026-05-13
box_source.rule: Extent of every vertex, minus/plus 0.15 degrees (the margin of map_sets.state in derived/packs/pack-spec.json), rounded outward to 0.01 degrees (floor for west and south, ceiling for east and north).

regions.area_note: The official figure is usually given as 1,098,581 km2 (general knowledge); the difference was not investigated.
regions.clip: Geofabrik's extract is cut a few kilometres outside the border, so a first build holds almost nothing of the neighbours and cuts the twin towns (general knowledge: Desaguadero, Puerto Quijarro/Corumbá, Guayaramerín/Guajará-Mirim, Cobija/Brasiléia, Villazón/La Quiaca, Yacuiba/Salvador Mazza). Suggested: the border as the edge of a first build; a band later. Undecided.

neighbours_in_box.method: Share of the box with margin, sampled on a 0.02 degree grid against Natural Earth 5.1.1 10 m admin-1 polygons (computed 2026-11-21). Shares of the box, not of km2; approximate.

alternative_regions.about: If finer regions are wanted: the nine departments. Each large city lies inside its own department (general knowledge), so a department map would not cut a metropolitan area.

box_source.dataset: OCHA COD-AB Bolivia (bol_admin0.geojson / bol_admin1.geojson from bol_admin_boundaries.geojson.zip), source Ministerio de Desarrollo Rural y Tierras, version v02, valid_on 2024-09-16, files last modified 2026-05-13
box_source.rule: Extent of every vertex, minus/plus 0.15 degrees (the margin of map_sets.state in derived/packs/pack-spec.json), rounded outward to 0.01 degrees (floor for west and south, ceiling for east and north).

alternative_regions.neighbours_method: As for BO: 0.02 degree grid against Natural Earth 5.1.1 10 m admin-1. The Bolivian share includes other Bolivian departments.

geoboundaries.dataset: geoBoundaries gbOpen BOL ADM0 and ADM1, source "GeoBolivia, Derived from ADM3 layer", year represented 2015, built 2023-12-12
geoboundaries.result: Every box equals COD-AB to four decimals (unrounded extents differ by less than 0.000001 degrees). The files appear to share the same geometry (an inference from the match), so this is not an independent check.

natural_earth.dataset: Natural Earth 5.1.1, 10 m admin-0 and admin-1
natural_earth.result: Largest edge difference from COD-AB: 0.0914 degrees (Tarija west, about 9.4 km); country box at most 0.0213 degrees (west). Every Natural Earth department box lies inside the COD-AB box with margin.

geofabrik_poly.result: Looser than COD-AB on all four sides, by 0.01 to 0.03 degrees.

boundary_caveats.water_holes: COD-AB levels 2 and 3 leave seven water features as holes (among them Salar de Uyuni, Salar de Coipasa, Lago Titicaca, Lago Poopó, Lago Uru Uru); levels 0 and 1, used for the boxes, enclose them (HDX caveat, opened).
boundary_caveats.internal_limits: Ley 339/2013 distinguishes "límites precisos" from "límites imprecisos" and sends demarcation to the IGM case by case (opened on Lexivox). Department lines are approximate in places; a box is only a cut for a download.

base_map_and_poi.dataset: OSM extract bolivia-latest.osm.pbf (167 MB as Geofabrik shows it; bolivia-261120.osm.pbf is 175,175,057 bytes); -free.shp.zip 396 MB, -free.gpkg.zip 405 MB

places.dataset: OCHA COD-AB levels 1 to 3 (9 departments, 112 provinces, 339 municipalities) and adminpoints; OSM named places
places.verified: HDX record opened 2026-11-21; unit counts computed from the GeoJSON

terrain.verified: as in docs/regions-proposed.json; Bolivian tiles not checked

buildings.dataset: Google Open Buildings v3 (BOL in its country list, "subject to change"); Microsoft Global ML Building Footprints (238 Bolivia tiles in dataset-links.csv of 2026-11-12)
buildings.verified: both pages opened 2026-11-21; coverage and quality not measured
buildings.notes: Google: CC BY 4.0 or ODbL 1.0, at the user's choice. Microsoft: CDLA Permissive 2.0.

addresses.gap: Overture's address theme (release 2026-11-18.0) lists 41 countries and Bolivia is not among them. OSM has 10,527 objects with addr:housenumber.

hazards.dataset: SENAMHI alerts, flood extents, heat spots and drought monitor (senamhi.gob.bo)
hazards.verified: home page and three sub-pages opened 2026-11-21; data not read (JavaScript)

osm_counts.about: Counted with pyosmium over bolivia-261120.osm.pbf (MD5 a142ed996037a4005a68196ad154f036, matching Geofabrik; data up to 2026-11-20T21:21:21Z); nodes, ways and relations. Rows, not sites.

addr_housenumber_by_department.about: Nodes, and ways by their first node; relations not placed. Departments from COD-AB level 1.

osm_counts.caveat: amenity=shelter marks small roofs, not emergency shelters. healthcare=* overlaps amenity=* and was not de-duplicated.

help_point_gaps.health: No Ministry of Health facility download found. HDX: hotosm_bol_health_facilities (OSM, ODbL, 2026-11-16) and bolivia-healthsites (OSM, ODbL, 2026-09-29) are OSM data; bolivia-health (Ministerio de Salud y Deportes, licence "Other", 2018-08-16) is old with unclear terms.

legal_open_question.summary: No Bolivian rule like Chile's DIFROL legend was found, but the search was incomplete. Left to the maintainers.
legal_open_question.ley_339_2013: Art. 23: "La cartografía oficial es aquella elaborada por el Instituto Geográfico Militar"; Art. 16: the IGM "no define la delimitación de unidades territoriales" (opened on Lexivox, unofficial copy, 2026-11-21).
legal_open_question.ds_5050_2023: Approves the internal boundary layer and sends limits to the IGM for demarcation (opened in an earlier pass on 2026-11-21; not reopened).
legal_open_question.igm_terms: Not checked: igm.gob.bo and igmbolivia.gob.bo gave no answer.
legal_open_question.sea_claim: Bolivia keeps a claim to access to the Pacific; the ICJ ruled in 2018 that Chile has no obligation to negotiate (general knowledge). No rule found that maps must show it (search only). DS 5376 of 2025-04-16 closed the Dirección Estratégica de Reivindicación Marítima, Silala y Recursos Hídricos Internacionales (opened on Lexivox).

emergency_numbers.about: Recorded only so the map and the number table agree; the table belongs to issue #261. No number is proposed for the app or for guide search.

addressing.order: Street, then number, then zona or barrio and city; "s/n" for no number (general knowledge).
addressing.postcode: Not in everyday use (general knowledge, not checked).
addressing.accents: normalize() in engine/address_search.py turns "Potosí" into "potos" and "Calle Ñuflo de Chávez Nº 123" into "calle uflo de ch vez n 123" (tested 2026-11-22). See related.pr_79.
addressing.osm_addresses: addr:housenumber on 10,527 objects; 4,581 in La Paz, 2,939 in Cochabamba, 2,282 in Santa Cruz, 629 in the other six departments (computed).
addressing.verified: No Bolivian postal or municipal source checked; needs a Bolivian reader.
